All database/table names used in the f-string-built DDL/SQL (database_name, table_name, dst_table, model_db, model_table, tokenizer_table, vector_db, chunk_embed_table) come from server-side rag_config.yml (RAG_CONFIG), not from the caller. question is inserted only via bound '?' placeholders (rag_tools.py lines 267-282, 400-415), never string-formatted into SQL. k is declared int and, per fastmcp 3.4.7's pydantic-based argument validation (installed at eval/targets/Teradata__mcp-server/.venv/.../fastmcp/tools/function_parsing.py), cannot carry a non-numeric string into the f'TopK({k})' interpolation in build_search_query (rag_tools.py line 102).
role_name is bound as SQLAlchemy :role_name (sec_objects.yml lines 20-97); no string interpolation.
user_name is bound as SQLAlchemy :user_name (sec_objects.yml lines 1-18); no string interpolation.
user_name is bound as SQLAlchemy :user_name inside a LIKE '%' || :user_name || '%' concatenation (sec_objects.yml lines 99-118); the bind value itself is still parameterized, not string-formatted.

sort_by_metric is validated against a fixed valid_metrics allowlist and silently reset to the safe default 'avg_cpu' if it isn't a member (sql_opt_tools.py lines 564-578) before being spliced into ORDER BY/RANK() OVER (ORDER BY {sort_by_metric} ...) at lines 615-623; limit_results is declared int (guarded by fastmcp/pydantic type coercion, verified against the installed fastmcp 3.4.7 in .venv) before being spliced into 'TOP {limit_results}' at line 582. feature_db/stats_table come from server config, not the caller.

feature_db/model_db/model_id and all table names are sourced from SQL_CLUSTERING_CONFIG (server-side sql_opt_config.yml), not the caller. The only caller-controlled parameters, optimal_k and max_queries, are declared int and used solely in numeric SQL positions (NumClusters({optimal_k}), <= {max_queries}); fastmcp 3.4.7's pydantic-based validation (installed .venv) rejects non-numeric input before the handler runs.

metric is validated against a fixed valid_metrics allowlist and reset to the safe default 'ampcputime' if it isn't a member (sql_opt_tools.py lines 732-746) before being spliced into ORDER BY/QUALIFY clauses; cluster_ids is declared list[int] and limit_per_cluster is declared int, both guarded by fastmcp/pydantic type coercion (verified against the installed fastmcp 3.4.7 in .venv) before cluster_ids_str=','.join(map(str,cluster_ids)) is spliced into an IN (...) clause. feature_db/clusters_table come from server config, not the caller.
